claim: The restriction on else departs from the general rule that, syntactically, the order of post-head internal dependents is completely free (see §15).
evidence_summary: §15, p. 454: “Although the order of post-head internal dependents is essentially labile, certain specialised types are subject to rigid ordering constraints”. Its rule [14] includes else before restrictors.
finding: The §9.6 restriction is one of the rigid constraints §15 recognizes. General rule and from a syntactic point of view partly rescue the sentence. Two readers weighed it differently.
proposed_wording: departs from the general lability of post-head internal dependents (see §15)
inference: Is post-head order free apart from this restriction?

evidence.establishes: The cross-referenced section states rigid constraints.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
